newsitem.title: BURMA: Former Burmese strongman Saw Maung dead at 69.
newsitem.headline: Former Burmese strongman Saw Maung dead at 69.

text.p: General Saw Maung, who chaired Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) when it was set up in 1988, died of a heart attack on Thursday at his residence, a government statement said.
The brief statement gave no further details except that Saw Maung had died at his residence early in the morning.
Saw Maung, 69, led the military to power by crushing a mass democracy uprising in September 1988.
The military killed thousands of people that year and the junta run by Saw Maung arrested thousands of opponents to the regime, including Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
Saw Maung, born in Mandalay on May 12, 1928, was army chief of staff and defence minister before leading the coup and becoming chairman of the SLORC on September 18, 1988.
Shortly after seizing power, Saw Maung vowed to hold multi-party elections, but also said the army's first priority was to "restore law and order and peace and tranquility".
The elections were held in 1990 but never recognised after Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy party won them by a landslide.
Saw Maung was a protege of former strongman Ne Win and was thought to have led the 1988 coup under his orders.
Ne Win, who is still alive, was the much-feared architect of authoritarian rule who led Burma for more than a quarter century under the ill-fated Burmese Way to Socialism doctrine.

Saw Maung gave up his defence portfolio in March 1992 and stepped down as SLORC chairman on April 23, 1992 because of ill health. He was replaced by his former assistant and the current prime minister, Senior General Than Shwe.

Saw Maung, who was rumoured to have suffered a nervous breakdown, had behaved erratically in public following the 1991 awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize to Suu Kyi and the international condemnation that followed.
He was also thought to have a drinking problem, to be suffering from diabetes and a heart condition.
Saw Maung was educated to the high school level and joined the army in 1948. He was given his first major post of vice-chief of staff of the army and deputy minister of defence in 1984.
He became commander in chief of the armed forces in April 1985 and was promoted to general the following year. Saw Mung became Minister of Defence in July 1988,
He was survived by his wife, Aye Yee, and their two daughters and one son.
